summary:
I fixed the checker's should item (T1) and two of its nits (T2, T3). I left N1 alone. Every change is in tools/smoke.js in /home/user/ppolppol-fix-v2. No game code changed: js/app.js, js/salon.js and tools/test-salon.js are exactly as the first fix left them. Nothing is committed.

- **T1 (should):** a new Q check, 23-1b. It seeds a production week where the '선물 상자에서 하나 내밀기' slot was not done (n 0) and four other tasks were done. It expects (4/5), no keptIds, no claim button, no dot and no kept line. On the next Monday it expects no week.prev and only that day's gift (shells 20 to 23). The current code passes. The checker's mutant MD (`>= 1` changed to `>= 0` in GONE.gift) now fails this check.
- **T3 (nit):** a new Q check, 23-1c. It seeds a week where every slot is a current task and the save holds keptIds ['days','days'] with kept 3, plus three tasks really done. It expects (4/5) with no claim button. Mutant MB (weekDoneN reads the kept number) and mutant MC (no dedupe) now each fail it.
- **T2 (nit):** both late-write checks in X now freeze performance.now() during the call. In each, the stale record is sent in the same call as the import, so the result no longer depends on machine speed.
  - The older check: the import and the stale record now go in one call.
  - The newer check: it captures its own stale record ('구름') inside that call, instead of the window.__xpre that the earlier reload had wiped. It now asserts that this record was really there and really dropped.
  - Mutant MF0 (IMPORT_HOLD = 0) now fails both checks.
  - A control copy waited 1.5 s in a busy loop right after each import and still passed 51/0, which shows the checks do not depend on speed.

Final suites on the final tree (load 2.4 to 4.1 on 4 CPUs):
- SMOKE_ONLY=Q: 73/0 three times in a row.
- SMOKE_ONLY=X: 51/0 three times in a row.
- SMOKE_ONLY=A: 74/0.
- SMOKE_ONLY=Y: 99/0. This is the first clean Y run for this lane; the first fixer's two Y runs crashed under heavy load.
- npm test: 0 failed.
- Font check: stale none.

No player-facing text changed.

changes.lines: 5986-6006 (X section 9: im2 / im3 and their assertion)
changes.what: Removed the window.__xpre capture. im2 now reads the pre-import record, freezes performance.now(), runs the import, dispatches the stale record in the same call, records what this tab shows, and restores the clock in finally. im3 now only sends the newer record. The assertion now reads the stale result from im2, and also checks that the stale record really held shells 40.

changes.lines: 6042-6058 (end of X section 9, the C4/C6/C2 step g1)
changes.what: g1 now captures the record stored before the import inside the call ('구름', lastSeen set to Date.now()-1). It freezes performance.now() from before the import through the stale dispatch and restores both hooks in finally. It asserts late.pre === '구름' and that the tab still shows the imported '뚜루' with shells 21. The inHold timing flag is gone.
changes.why: T2: window.__xpre was undefined after the earlier pa.reload(), so the dispatch did nothing and this half of the check held whatever the guard did.

decisions:
T2: I froze performance.now() inside the call instead of only merging the calls. Merging alone still leaves a speed dependence: under heavy load, the import plus its render could itself take more than 1 s. With the clock frozen, 'right after the import' holds on any machine, and the real hold rule (IMPORT_HOLD) still decides the result. MF0 shows this: with the hold set to 0, both checks fail.

In g1 I set the stale record's lastSeen to Date.now()-1, read just before the import. That makes it certainly older than importSeen even if earlier saves pushed lastSeen a few ms ahead of the wall clock. In im2 I kept the raw stored record unchanged, as the older check did; it is written in an earlier call, so it is older than the import.

T3: I added the check the checker suggested. It costs one browser context and is cheap.

T1: I reused 23-1's week so the only difference from the 'done gift' case is n 0.

N1: left alone. It is not from this change (6d03faf behaves the same), it is outside the brief's items, and points are already counted once. Keeping a re-dealt slot's rr would also change the rerolls a production slot gets in the new build. That is a visible behaviour change and not clearly safe to make in a repair round.

How I ran the Q mutant runs: on a /dev/shm copy with a temporary hook line after FIVE that runs only qGone. The hook was never in the real tree, and the copy is deleted.
